What counts as an HVAC emergency?

Not every hiccup is urgent, but some problems should be handled right away to protect your home, your equipment, and your family’s comfort.

Cooling emergencies

  • AC not turning on and indoor temps rising
  • Warm air blowing when the thermostat is set to cool
  • Frequent tripping of the breaker for the AC
  • Ice on the refrigerant lines or outdoor unit
  • Burning smell or electrical odor from the air handler
  • Water leaking from the indoor unit or ceiling
  • Loud banging, screeching, or grinding noises

Heating emergencies

  • Furnace not firing on a cold night
  • Heat pump stuck in cooling or not heating well
  • Repeated short cycling and safety lockouts
  • Burning or electrical smells
  • Strange noises from the blower or burner area
  • Carbon monoxide alarm sounding
  • Pilot will not stay lit or igniter clicks but no flame

Airflow and duct problems

  • Almost no airflow in parts of the home
  • Sudden rise in dust, allergies, or musty odors
  • A collapsed, disconnected, or blocked duct
  • Condensation or water dripping from supply vents

If you smell gas, leave the building right away and call 911 or SDG&E. Once your space is safe, we can fix the HVAC issue that caused the concern.

Fast response across San Diego County

Where are you located? Our techs know San Diego streets, shortcuts, and traffic. We get to you quickly and keep you updated along the way.

  • Central includes Downtown, Little Italy, Mission Valley, Hillcrest, North Park, Golden Hill
  • Coastal includes La Jolla, Pacific Beach, Ocean Beach, Point Loma, Clairemont, Bay Park

Heat spikes, Santa Ana winds, the marine layer, and coastal corrosion can be tough on equipment. We plan for that with parts and tools that match local conditions. A summer breakdown in Mission Valley can feel different from a night call in Rancho Bernardo. We have done both plenty of times.

What to try before you call

Want a quick win? A few safe steps might get you going or at least give us clues so we fix it faster.

  • Check the thermostat. Set it to cool or heat and at least 3 degrees beyond the current room temperature. Replace the batteries if it has them.
  • Look at the breaker panel. Reset any tripped breaker for the furnace, air handler, or condenser. If it trips again, stop and call us.
  • Inspect the air filter. A clogged filter can choke airflow and freeze coils. Replace the filter if it is dirty.
  • Peek at the outdoor unit. Remove leaves or debris around the condenser. Keep at least 2 feet of clearance.
  • Check for ice. If you see ice on the refrigerant lines, turn the system off and set the fan to On to help thaw. Running a frozen system can cause damage.
  • Look for water. If you see water near the indoor unit, turn off the system. A clogged condensate drain can overflow and damage ceilings or floors.

If there is a burning smell, gas odor, or visible sparking, shut off power at the breaker, leave the area, and call for help. Safety first.

Our emergency repair process

Clear steps get you from stress to relief.

  • 1) You call. We listen. We ask simple questions to understand symptoms, location, and access. If you need after-hours help, we flag it for priority dispatch.
  • 2) We dispatch. A tech calls you on the way and shares an arrival window. Traffic on the 5 or 15 can be rough, so we keep you updated.
  • 3) We diagnose. We run tests, check components, and track the real cause. We do not guess and swap parts without a plan. Professional diagnostics guide every decision.
  • 4) You get pricing. We present the repair options and price before any work starts. No surprise fees later.
  • 5) We fix it. Our vehicles carry common parts for ACs, furnaces, and heat pumps. Most repairs are finished on the first visit. Need non-emergency work later? See our HVAC System Repair options.
  • 6) We test and clean up. We verify the system cycles properly, check airflow and temperatures, and leave the area tidy.
  • 7) You get tips. We show you what went wrong and how to avoid a repeat. If a maintenance visit or duct cleaning would help, we explain why and let you decide.

Common emergency fixes we handle today

You do not need to know every part name. Still, it helps to understand what might be going on. Here are the usual suspects we see across San Diego.

AC repairs

  • Failed capacitor or contactor that keeps the outdoor unit from starting
  • Burned blower motor or seized bearings
  • Refrigerant leak that caused low pressure and warm air
  • Clogged condensate drain that drips through ceilings in Mission Valley condos
  • Frozen evaporator coil from low airflow or low refrigerant
  • Faulty thermostat or failed control board
  • Dirty condenser coil after a dusty Santa Ana week

Heat pump fixes

  • Reversing valve stuck and not switching between heat and cool
  • Defrost control issues on chilly, damp mornings in coastal areas
  • Low refrigerant leading to weak heat output
  • Outdoor fan motor failure or iced over outdoor unit

Furnace repairs

  • Igniter or flame sensor failure
  • Dirty burners causing rough start and noisy flames
  • Faulty inducer motor and pressure switch errors
  • Limit switch trips from clogged filter or blocked vents
  • Intermittent pilot issues on older systems

Duct and airflow repairs

  • Disconnected or crushed flexible duct in the attic
  • Return duct leaks pulling dusty attic air into the home
  • Closed or blocked registers causing hot and cold spots
  • Blower wheel packed with dust and pet hair, cutting airflow

Thermostats and controls

  • Older thermostats with failing relays or sensors
  • Wi‑Fi thermostat settings or schedule conflicts after power blips
  • Bad wiring connections at the furnace or air handler

Electrical and safety

  • Shorted wires from rodents in attics or crawl spaces
  • Breakers tripping from overloaded circuits
  • Loose lugs or burned connections inside the disconnect

We fix the cause, not just the symptom, so you are not calling again next week. If needed, we can also perform HVAC Troubleshooting to track down intermittent issues.

Same-day replacements when repair does not make sense

Sometimes the repair cost is close to the value of the old unit. If your system is past its best years, we can quote a replacement that fits your space, budget, and timeline. We handle emergency swaps with proper sizing, safe installation, and fast turnaround, so you are not stuck for days. You get options with clear pricing, then you choose.

Local scenarios we solve every week

San Diego has its own mix of weather and housing styles. That mix creates predictable HVAC trouble. Here are situations we face often.

  • Coastal corrosion In Ocean Beach and Point Loma salty air can corrode capacitors and outdoor coils. The AC clicks but does not start. We test, replace the failed part, and rinse the coil to extend life.
  • East County heat In El Cajon and Santee heat loads are high. Weak airflow plus a dirty filter can freeze the coil. We thaw, fix the cause, and get you cooling again before the home turns into an oven.
  • Mission Valley leaks Condensate lines clog and overflow onto ceilings. We clear the drain, flush with treatment, and install a float switch if needed to shut the system off before it leaks next time.
  • North Park classics Older homes have undersized returns and long duct runs. A furnace can overheat and lock out. We restore airflow, clean the blower, and balance the system so it runs steady.
  • Chula Vista cold snaps A chilly morning hits and the furnace will not light. The flame sensor is dirty. We clean or replace the sensor, check burners, and confirm safe operation.
  • Power blips After SDG&E outages, heat pumps and smart thermostats sometimes get confused. We reset the system, update settings, and verify normal operation.
  • Smoke and air quality During brush fire season homes fill with odor even with the windows closed. We set systems to recirculate, install higher MERV filters temporarily, and seal duct leaks to reduce smoke infiltration.

Does one of these sound familiar? We can help today. Call {{phone}}.

Safety first, always

HVAC issues mix electricity, gas, water, and moving parts. A few reminders help keep everyone safe.

  • Gas smell means get out right away and call 911 or SDG&E
  • If you see smoke or sparks, cut power at the breaker and step away
  • Do not reach into equipment while it is powered
  • Keep children and pets away from the work area
  • Water near electrical gear is risky, so shut off power and call us

Tell us what you see and smell. Those details guide our next steps and keep the visit efficient.

Indoor air quality during an emergency

Comfort is not only temperature. If your system is struggling, indoor air can take a hit too.

  • Dust bursts after a filter collapse
  • Musty odors from wet insulation or clogged drains
  • Smoke infiltration during regional fires
  • Allergy flare-ups when duct leaks pull attic air into the home

We can stabilize air quality while we restore cooling or heating. That might include a quick duct seal at a disconnected joint, a fresh filter with higher efficiency using our Media Filter Installation, or a blower and coil cleaning if they are packed with debris. Once the emergency is handled, we can plan deeper cleaning or duct sealing to help prevent a repeat.

Maintenance that prevents late night calls

No one wants another emergency visit. Regular maintenance reduces surprise breakdowns and helps systems run efficiently during heat waves and cold snaps.

  • Seasonal tune-ups to catch weak parts before they fail
  • Drain cleaning to prevent ceiling leaks
  • Coil cleaning for steadier cooling
  • Airflow checks and static pressure tests
  • Thermostat calibration and programming help

Since Sky Clean Air also cleans ducts, we can pair a tune-up with duct inspection. Sealing leaks and improving return airflow often brings temperatures back in line across the home and eases the load on the system.

Signs you should call now

Not sure if you should wait or pick up the phone? If you see any of these, reach out right away.

  • System is off and the home is heating up or cooling down fast
  • Breaker keeps tripping
  • Burning smell or smoke
  • Water leaking at the indoor unit
  • Carbon monoxide alarm is sounding
  • You have very young kids, elderly family, or health concerns and the home is uncomfortable

We will guide you on next steps and send help quickly.

If you want to see the failed part, we are glad to show it. If you want the short version and cold air pronto, we get right to it.

Your duct cleaning pros who also run great emergency calls

Why does duct experience matter during an emergency? Airflow is half the battle. Many breakdowns start with restricted air. Frozen coils, overheated furnaces, noisy blowers, and hot rooms often point to airflow problems that hide in the duct system.

Sky Clean Air pairs emergency HVAC repairs with a trained eye on the ducts. We find and fix the cause, not just the symptom, which saves you time and money.

A few final tips from the field

These simple habits reduce breakdowns and keep energy bills in check.

  • Replace your filter every 1 to 3 months, more often if you have pets or frequent construction dust
  • Keep 2 feet of space around the outdoor unit and trim back plants
  • Do not close too many supply vents, even in unused rooms
  • Set your thermostat and resist constant changes that cause short cycling
  • Consider a spring and fall tune-up so surprises do not land at the worst time

We love meeting our neighbors, just not at 1 a.m. for a flooded ceiling. A little care goes a long way.

Yes, Sky Clean Air provides emergency service for air conditioning issues.

Sky Clean Air can assist with heating problems at any time, including nights and weekends.
